claim: BAP learns fault localization by probing an LLM's attention patterns via weak supervision, explicitly without requiring executable test cases or direct line-level localization labels.
stance_target: BAP occupies the per-test-execution-verifiability mechanism of the proposed paper
quoted_support: Existing FL approaches rely on executable test cases, require training on costly and often noisy line-level annotations, or demand resource-intensive LLMs... BAP, a method which learns state-of-the-art fault localization without any direct localization labels.

claim: BAP is evaluated via Top-1/Top-N line-localization accuracy across 8 datasets, never AUROC or a calibration metric; it improves 34.6% top-1 accuracy over the strongest FL baseline and 93.4% over zero-shot GPT-4o prompting.
quoted_support: Averaged across all eight datasets, BAP improves by 34.6% top-1 accuracy compared to the strongest baseline and 93.4% over zero-shot prompting GPT-4o.

claim: BAP's confidence/localization signal derives from probing model-internal attention weights of a separate probe, not from the code-generating LLM's own expressed/self-reported confidence.
stance_target: BAP occupies the proposed paper's self-expressed confidence mechanism
quoted_support: we present Bug Attention Probe (BAP), a method which learns state-of-the-art fault localization without any direct localization labels, outperforming traditional FL baselines and prompting of large-scale LLMs.
